doc_paragraphs.text: ResearchLoop is a SaaS MVP for executing and monitoring autonomous AI research loops. It collects sources, extracts factual claims, cross-examines statements for contradictions, surfaces open questions, and compiles synthesized research reports — all isolated per user via Supabase Row Level Security.

- **Framework**: Next.js (App Router, React Server Components) - **Language**: TypeScript - **Styling**: Tailwind CSS v4 - **UI Primitives**: Radix UI + Lucide icons (custom dark theme) - **Database & Auth**: Supabase (PostgreSQL, cookie-based SSR sessions, RLS) - **Background jobs**: [Trigger.dev](https://trigger.dev) v4 (project ref `proj_pjaribdquznpuxwkpuyq`). Long-running deep research runs in Trigger.dev tasks, not in web requests. A development-only simulated runner is the local fallback when Trigger.dev is not configured (see [Background research jobs](#background-research-jobs)).
The repo is aligned to the **live** Supabase project (the source of truth). The baseline migration in [`supabase/migrations`](./supabase/migrations) was reconstructed by inspecting the live database.

**The live database has exactly 10 public tables.** There is **no `profiles` table** and **no `run_steps` table** (earlier drafts of this repo incorrectly described a 12-table schema — that has been corrected).

| # | Table | Purpose | | --- | -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | 1 | `projects` | Workspace containers grouping research activity. | | 2 | `research_questions` | The question/objective driving a loop (`question`, `depth`, `modes`, …). | | 3 | `research_runs` | A run instance. Status: `queued`/`running`/`complete`/`failed`/`cancelled`. Holds `cost_estimate` and a `metadata` JSONB. | | 4 | `provider_runs` | LLM adapter call metadata (`provider`, `model`, `token_usage_json`, `cost_estimate`). | | 5 | `sources` | Collected sources (`title`, `url`, `publisher`, `published_date`, `credibility_score`). | | 6 | `claims` | Extracted factual statements (`claim_text`, `evidence_strength`, `confidence_score`, `source_ids`). | | 7 | `contradictions` | Conflicts between claims (`claim_a`, `claim_b`, `severity`, `status`). | | 8 | `open_questions` | Knowledge gaps (`question`, `priority`, `should_trigger_loop`). | | 9 | `reports` | Final synthesized markdown packets (`title`, `report_type`, `markdown_content`). | | 10 | `research_loops` | Links a parent run + open question to a foll

- **`profiles` exists?** No. User identity comes from Supabase Auth (`auth.users`); each table carries a `user_id` referencing `auth.users(id)`. - **`run_steps` exists?** No. The execution **timeline and logs are stored in `research_runs.metadata`** (JSONB) under `metadata.steps`. This keeps the repo aligned with the live database with no extra table. - **RLS**: enabled on all 10 tables, with four per-command policies each (`auth.uid() = user_id`). - **Triggers**: every table has a `set_updated_at` `BEFORE UPDATE` trigger. - **IDs**: `gen_random_uuid()` (pgcrypto). - **Status values** use `complete` (not `completed`) and there is no `partial`.

None. The baseline migration matches the live database; there are no pending additive migrations awaiting approval. (If a future feature needs a dedicated `run_steps` table, add it as a clearly-marked, separate, not-yet-applied migration rather than editing the baseline.)

- One **private** bucket: `researchloop-files`, folder convention `{user_id}/{project_id}/filename`, with SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policies restricting access to the authenticated user's own first folder segment. - The app does not currently upload files; the bucket is provisioned for future use. - ⚠️ The live project also contains an unrelated **public** bucket named `tickets`. It is **not** part of ResearchLoop — review and remove it if it is not needed (see the production checklist).

``` ResearchLoop/ ├── app/ # Next.js App Router views & layouts │ ├── (auth)/ # /login │ └── (dashboard)/ # /dashboard, /projects/* ├── components/ # UI modules (dashboard, project, run, ui) ├── lib/ │ ├── supabase/ # Browser, server, service-role, middleware clients │ └── providers/ # Research provider interface + mock + adapter scaffold ├── server/actions/ # Server actions (project CRUD, runs, simulated runner) ├── trigger/ # Trigger.dev tasks (research-run, research-loop) ├── trigger.config.ts # Trigger.dev config (project ref + task dir) ├── supabase/migrations/ # Baseline SQL migration + advisor hardening (match live DB) ├── types/ │ ├── supabase.ts # Generated Database type (from the live schema) │ └── index.ts # Domain types derived from Database └── middleware.ts # Auth route guarding ```
To inspect/verify the live database from an MCP-enabled assistant, configure the Supabase MCP server (read-only is recommended for inspection):

```jsonc // .mcp.json / client MCP config { "mcpServers": { "supabase": { "command": "npx", "args": [ "-y", "@supabase/mcp-server-supabase@latest", "--read-only", "--project-ref=<your-project-ref>", ], "env": { "SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN": "<personal-access-token>" }, }, }, } ```

1. **Configure `.env.local`** — copy `.env.example` to `.env.local` and fill in: ```bash cp .env.example .env.local ``` Set `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` (frontend- safe, from Supabase Dashboard > Project Settings > API). For the in-process simulated runner you can leave `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` and `TRIGGER_SECRET_KEY` empty. To run the **real Trigger.dev** task locally, set both and run `npm run trigger:dev` (see [Background research jobs](#background-research-jobs)). To run real OpenAI-backed research, also set: ```bash RESEARCH_PROVIDERS=openai OPENAI_API_KEY=... OPENAI_RESEARCH_MODEL=gpt-4.1 ``` `OPENAI_API_KEY` is server-only. Keep it in `.env.local` locally and add the same provider env vars to the Trigger.dev dashboard environment for real worker runs. To add Perplexity Sonar research, set: ```bash RESEARCH_PROVIDERS=openai,perplexity PERPLEXITY_API_KEY=... PERPLEXITY_RESEARCH_MODEL=sonar-deep-research ``` `PERPLEXITY_API_KEY` is server-only too. Add it locally and in the Trigger.dev dashboard environment. Perplexity is optional; if its key is missing, the registry skips it safely. `sonar-deep-research` can be expensive, so start with qui
The committed `types/supabase.ts` is generated from the live schema. To regenerate after a schema change (requires the Supabase CLI and a linked project via `supabase link --project-ref <ref>`):
```bash npm run gen:types # equivalently: # supabase gen types typescript --linked --schema public > types/supabase.ts ```

1. **Auth** (`/login`): sign up (or sign in). If using Supabase Cloud, either confirm the email or disable email confirmations to log in immediately. On success you land on `/dashboard`. 2. **Project CRUD**: create a project from the dashboard, edit it under _Workspace Settings_, and optionally delete it. 3. **Research question + queued run**: in a project's _Launch Loop_ tab, enter a question and submit. This inserts a `research_questions` row and a queued `research_runs` row, then redirects to the run detail page. 4. **Run detail / timeline / logs**: the run page polls and renders the timeline stepper, console logs (from `research_runs.metadata.steps`), and the structured output tabs (report, sources, claims, contradictions, open questions).

1. The user creates a project/question and launches a run. 2. The `triggerResearchRun` server action inserts a `research_questions` row and a `queued` `research_runs` row in Supabase. 3. It triggers the Trigger.dev **`research-run`** task (`trigger/research-run.ts`), passing the run/user/project/question ids. 4. The task calls the configured research provider(s), then writes results back to Supabase: `provider_runs`, `sources`, `claims`, `contradictions`, `open_questions`, `reports`, and (for open questions flagged to loop) a queued `research_loops` row. It updates `research_runs.status` (`running` → `complete`/`failed`) and stores the step timeline in `research_runs.metadata.steps`. 5. The run detail page reads status/results from Supabase (polling) — it never depends on an in-memory process.
Repeatable loops are handled by the **`research-loop`** task (`trigger/research-loop.ts`): it spawns a child run for an open question and hands it to `research-run`.

| Environment | `TRIGGER_SECRET_KEY` set? | Behaviour | | ----------- | ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Local dev | no | Falls back to the in-process **simulated runner** (`server/actions/run-executor.ts`) so you can develop without a Trigger.dev account. | | Local dev | yes (+ `npm run trigger:dev`) | Real Trigger.dev `research-run` task executes. | | Production | yes | Real Trigger.dev task executes. | | Production | no | Runs fail fast with a clear configuration error — the app never runs workers in-process in production. |
Failures from providers and tasks are always caught and persisted to `provider_runs.error_message` / `research_runs.error_message` — never silently ignored.

Providers implement the `ResearchProvider` interface in `lib/providers/`. The development/test default is a deterministic, offline **mock** provider (clearly-labelled placeholder output — no fake external data). Production defaults to real providers and will not fall back to mock output unless `ALLOW_MOCK_PROVIDER=true` is explicitly set. Select providers with the `RESEARCH_PROVIDERS` env var (comma-separated, e.g. `openai`, `openai,perplexity`, or `perplexity,mock` in allowed non-production runs). The OpenAI adapter lives in `lib/providers/openai-provider.ts` and uses the Responses API with web search and strict structured-output validation. The Perplexity adapter lives in `lib/providers/perplexity-provider.ts` and calls the Sonar API, then optionally uses OpenAI to normalize Perplexity's markdown report into the same structured provider output shape.
For OpenAI-backed runs, set these in local `.env.local` and in the Trigger.dev dashboard environment:
```bash RESEARCH_PROVIDERS=openai OPENAI_API_KEY=... OPENAI_RESEARCH_MODEL=gpt-4.1 ```
For Perplexity-backed runs, set these in local `.env.local` and in the Trigger.dev dashboard environment:
```bash RESEARCH_PROVIDERS=openai,perplexity PERPLEXITY_API_KEY=... PERPLEXITY_RESEARCH_MODEL=sonar-deep-research ```

Perplexity is optional. Unconfigured providers are skipped safely. In production, at least one real configured provider is required unless `ALLOW_MOCK_PROVIDER=true` is explicitly set for a non-customer test environment. `sonar-deep-research` can be expensive and slower than lightweight runs, so validate setup with quick or standard test runs before using deep runs.

If multiple providers are configured and one fails, the task persists that failure to `provider_runs`, records it in `research_runs.metadata`, and continues to the next provider. The whole run fails only when no provider produces output.

```bash # 1. Set TRIGGER_SECRET_KEY (dev key), SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, and any # provider vars such as OPENAI_API_KEY or PERPLEXITY_API_KEY in .env.local # 2. In one terminal: npm run dev # 3. In another terminal, start the Trigger.dev dev worker: npm run trigger:dev # = npx trigger.dev@latest dev ```
The first `trigger dev`/`deploy` opens a browser to log in to Trigger.dev and links this project (`proj_pjaribdquznpuxwkpuyq`, already set in `trigger.config.ts`).

Set the worker's environment variables (`SUPABASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, `RESEARCH_PROVIDERS`, and any provider keys such as `OPENAI_API_KEY` or `PERPLEXITY_API_KEY`) in the **Trigger.dev dashboard** for the matching environment. The worker uses the service-role key because it runs outside an authenticated request; it always writes the correct `user_id`.

- [ ] Configure production SMTP for auth emails. - [ ] Set `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` in Vercel production and set the Supabase **Site URL** to the same production domain. - [ ] Add production **redirect URLs** in Supabase Auth settings. - [ ] Set `TRIGGER_SECRET_KEY`, `SUPABASE_URL`, and `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` in the **Trigger.dev dashboard** environment, then `npm run trigger:deploy`. - [ ] Configure real research provider(s) via `RESEARCH_PROVIDERS`; OpenAI uses `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_RESEARCH_MODEL`, and Perplexity uses `PERPLEXITY_API_KEY` and `PERPLEXITY_RESEARCH_MODEL`. - [ ] **Review/remove the unused public `tickets` storage bucket** if it is not part of this product. - [ ] Verify `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` is server-only and never shipped to the browser (the app does not use it client-side).

```ts import { tasks } from "@trigger.dev/sdk"; import type { processData } from "./trigger/tasks";
// Single trigger const handle = await tasks.trigger<typeof processData>("process-data", { userId: "123", data: [{ id: 1 }, { id: 2 }], });

// Batch trigger (up to 1,000 items, 3MB per payload) const batchHandle = await tasks.batchTrigger<typeof processData>("process-data", [ { payload: { userId: "123", data: [{ id: 1 }] } }, { payload: { userId: "456", data: [{ id: 2 }] } }, ]); ```

```ts // Multiple rapid triggers with same key = single execution await myTask.trigger( { userId: "123" }, { debounce: { key: "user-123-update", // Unique key for debounce group delay: "5s", // Wait before executing }, } );

// Trailing mode: use payload from LAST trigger await myTask.trigger( { data: "latest-value" }, { debounce: { key: "trailing-example", delay: "10s", mode: "trailing", // Default is "leading" (first payload) }, } ); ```
**Debounce modes:** - `leading` (default): Uses payload from first trigger, subsequent triggers only reschedule - `trailing`: Uses payload from most recent trigger
```ts export const parentTask = task({ id: "parent-task", run: async (payload) => { // Trigger and continue const handle = await childTask.trigger({ data: "value" });

// Trigger and wait - returns Result object, NOT task output const result = await childTask.triggerAndWait({ data: "value" }); if (result.ok) { console.log("Task output:", result.output); // Actual task return value } else { console.error("Task failed:", result.error); }
// Quick unwrap (throws on error) const output = await childTask.triggerAndWait({ data: "value" }).unwrap();
// Batch trigger and wait const results = await childTask.batchTriggerAndWait([ { payload: { data: "item1" } }, { payload: { data: "item2" } }, ]);
for (const run of results) { if (run.ok) { console.log("Success:", run.output); } else { console.log("Failed:", run.error); } } }, });
export const childTask = task({ id: "child-task", run: async (payload: { data: string }) => { return { processed: payload.data }; }, }); ```

export const taskWithWaits = task({ id: "task-with-waits", run: async (payload) => { console.log("Starting task");
// Wait for specific duration await wait.for({ seconds: 30 }); await wait.for({ minutes: 5 }); await wait.for({ hours: 1 }); await wait.for({ days: 1 });
// Wait for token (from external system) await wait.forToken({ token: "user-approval-token", timeoutInSeconds: 3600, // 1 hour timeout });
> Never wrap wait calls in a Promise.all or Promise.allSettled as this is not supported in Trigger.dev tasks.

- **Result vs Output**: `triggerAndWait()` returns a `Result` object with `ok`, `output`, `error` properties - NOT the direct task output - **Type safety**: Use `import type` for task references when triggering from backend - **Waits > 5 seconds**: Automatically checkpointed, don't count toward compute usage - **Debounce + idempotency**: Idempotency keys take precedence over debounce settings

// Trigger with tags await processUser.trigger( { userId: "123", orgId: "abc" }, { tags: ["priority", "user_123", "org_abc"] } // Max 10 tags per run );
// Subscribe to tagged runs for await (const run of runs.subscribeToRunsWithTag("user_123")) { console.log(`User task ${run.id}: ${run.status}`); } ```
- Use prefixes: `user_123`, `org_abc`, `video:456` - Max 10 tags per run, 1-64 characters each - Tags don't propagate to child tasks automatically
- **Maximum batch size**: 1,000 items (increased from 500) - **Payload per item**: 3MB each (increased from 1MB combined) - Payloads > 512KB automatically offload to object storage
| Tier | Bucket Size | Refill Rate | |------|-------------|-------------| | Free | 1,200 runs | 100 runs/10 sec | | Hobby | 5,000 runs | 500 runs/5 sec | | Pro | 5,000 runs | 500 runs/5 sec |
| Tier | Concurrent Batches | |------|-------------------| | Free | 1 | | Hobby | 10 | | Pro | 10 |

// Batch trigger with wait const results = await myTask.batchTriggerAndWait([ { payload: { userId: "user-1" } }, { payload: { userId: "user-2" } }, ]);

Consolidate multiple triggers into a single execution by debouncing task runs with a unique key and delay window.

- **User activity updates**: Batch rapid user actions into a single run - **Webhook deduplication**: Handle webhook bursts without redundant processing - **Search indexing**: Combine document updates instead of processing individually - **Notification batching**: Group notifications to prevent user spam
```ts await myTask.trigger( { userId: "123" }, { debounce: { key: "user-123-update", // Unique identifier for debounce group delay: "5s", // Wait duration ("5s", "1m", or milliseconds) }, } ); ```
**Leading Mode** (default): Uses payload/options from the first trigger; subsequent triggers only reschedule execution time.
```ts // First trigger sets the payload await myTask.trigger({ action: "first" }, { debounce: { key: "my-key", delay: "10s" } });
// Second trigger only reschedules - payload remains "first" await myTask.trigger({ action: "second" }, { debounce: { key: "my-key", delay: "10s" } }); // Task executes with { action: "first" } ```
```ts await myTask.trigger( { data: "latest-value" }, { debounce: { key: "trailing-example", delay: "10s", mode: "trailing", }, } ); ```

In trailing mode, these options update with each trigger: - `payload` — task input data - `metadata` — run metadata - `tags` — run tags (replaces existing) - `maxAttempts` — retry attempts - `maxDuration` — maximum compute time - `machine` — machine preset
- Idempotency keys take precedence over debounce settings - Compatible with `triggerAndWait()` — parent runs block correctly on debounced execution - Debounce key is scoped to the task

// Per-user concurrency export const processUserData = task({ id: "process-user-data", run: async (payload: { userId: string }) => { // Override queue with user-specific concurrency await childTask.trigger(payload, { queue: { name: `user-${payload.userId}`, concurrencyLimit: 2, }, }); }, });
export const emailTask = task({ id: "send-email", queue: emailQueue, // Use shared queue run: async (payload: { to: string }) => { // Send email logic }, }); ```

export const resilientTask = task({ id: "resilient-task", retry: { maxAttempts: 10, factor: 1.8, // Exponential backoff multiplier minTimeoutInMs: 500, maxTimeoutInMs: 30_000, randomize: false, }, catchError: async ({ error, ctx }) => { // Custom error handling if (error.code === "FATAL_ERROR") { throw new AbortTaskRunError("Cannot retry this error"); }

// Allow retry by returning nothing return { retryAt: new Date(Date.now() + 60000) }; // Retry in 1 minute }, run: async (payload) => { // Retry specific operations const result = await retry.onThrow( async () => { return await unstableApiCall(payload); }, { maxAttempts: 3 } );

// Conditional HTTP retries const response = await retry.fetch("https://api.example.com", { retry: { maxAttempts: 5, condition: (response, error) => { return response?.status === 429 || response?.status >= 500; }, }, });

- **Concurrency**: Use queues to prevent overwhelming external services - **Retries**: Configure exponential backoff for transient failures - **Idempotency**: Always use for payment/critical operations - **Metadata**: Track progress for long-running tasks - **Machines**: Match machine size to computational requirements - **Tags**: Use consistent naming patterns for filtering - **Debouncing**: Use for user activity, webhooks, and notification batching - **Batch triggering**: Use for bulk operations up to 1,000 items - **Error Handling**: Distinguish between retryable and fatal errors
Design tasks to be stateless, idempotent, and resilient to failures. Use metadata for state tracking and queues for resource management.

Configure your local environment, point the app at a Supabase project, and run the ResearchLoop MVP.

> The **live Supabase database is the source of truth.** The repo's baseline > migration and generated types already match it (10 tables, no `profiles`, no > `run_steps`). If you stand up your own Supabase project, apply the baseline > migration to reproduce that schema.

- **Node.js**: 18.x or 20.x+ - **npm**: 9.x+ (or yarn/pnpm/bun) - **Supabase**: a project on [Supabase Cloud](https://supabase.com) **or** the [Supabase CLI](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/cli) (Docker) for a local stack.

1. Copy the example file: ```bash cp .env.example .env.local ``` 2. Fill in `.env.local` from **Supabase Dashboard > Project Settings > API**: - `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` — the project URL (frontend-safe). - `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` — the `anon` public key (frontend-safe; RLS constrains access). - `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` — canonical app URL, for example `https://your-app.vercel.app`. Set this in Vercel production so auth email redirects never fall back to localhost. - `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` — server-only; bypasses RLS and must never reach the browser. Required to run the real Trigger.dev worker (leave empty to use the in-process simulated runner locally). - `SUPABASE_URL` — same value as `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`; used by the Trigger.dev worker. Optional locally. - `TRIGGER_SECRET_KEY` — Trigger.dev dev/prod secret key. Leave empty locally to use the simulated runner; set it (and run `npm run trigger:dev`) to use the real `research-run` task. - `RESEARCH_PROVIDERS` / provider API keys / provider model vars — optional; select/configure research providers. For OpenAI-backed runs, set: ```bash RESEARCH_PROVIDERS=openai OPENAI_API_KEY=... OPENAI_RESEARCH_MODEL=gpt-4.1 ```

For real Trigger.dev execution, add the same provider env vars (`RESEARCH_PROVIDERS`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_RESEARCH_MODEL`, `PERPLEXITY_API_KEY`, `PERPLEXITY_RESEARCH_MODEL`) to the Trigger.dev dashboard environment as well.

The schema lives in [`supabase/migrations/20260530000000_init.sql`](./supabase/migrations/20260530000000_init.sql). It creates the 10 public tables, RLS policies, indexes, `set_updated_at` triggers, and the private `researchloop-files` storage bucket with owner-folder policies.

*Prepared June 12, 2026. Based on a full-codebase audit, live market research (June 2026 pricing verified against vendor docs), a four-lens strategic analysis (bear / bull / pricing-GTM / technical), and an adversarial cross-review of all findings.*
**Conditional yes — the codebase has real, salvageable commercial value, but not as the product it currently presents itself as.**

- As an "autonomous deep-research loop," ResearchLoop has **no value to sell**. The loop is a commodity: Google sells it as an API for ~$2/task, OpenAI for $0.41–$0.92 (o4-mini), Anthropic Managed Agents runs hosted iterate-grade-revise loops for $0.08/session-hour + tokens, and Google AI Pro gives consumers **20 deep-research runs per day for $19.99/month**. Nobody will pay a solo-developer SaaS to run a loop the platforms sell cheaper, faster, and under trusted brands. - As a **verification, audit, and persistence layer on top of commodity research APIs**, it is on the right side of the market's largest validated gap: the #1 documented pain with every deep-research product is citation hallucination (CJR measured >60% wrong citations across 8 generative search tools; fabricated academic references are up ~10× to 1-in-277), and enterprises pay $10K–$100K/year (AlphaSense, Crayon, Klue) for research they can *trust* — a 100–1000× premium over the $0.50–$3 API cost of generating it. That premium is paid for trust, accountability, and workflow, not generation. - The schema already shipped (May 30 migration) is the right substrate: every claim is a Postgres row with `evidence_strength`
**The honest one-line strategy: demote the loop to a swappable commodity backend, and sell "research you can defend."**

A critical caveat the adversarial review surfaced: today the trust artifacts (confidence scores, evidence strength, contradictions) are themselves generated by the same model class that hallucinates, with **zero measured accuracy**. Until a real verification pass exists and is benchmarked, the defensible positioning is **"auditable and reviewable"** — not "more accurate." Building and measuring actual citation verification is the make-or-break feature.

### What exists and works - Full auth → project → question → background run → results flow on Next.js 16 / Supabase / Vercel / Trigger.dev v4. - 4-stage pipeline in Trigger.dev workers: provider calls (Perplexity `sonar-deep-research`, OpenAI gpt-4.1 + web search) → claim extraction → contradiction detection + open-question generation → master report. Four levels of fallback persistence; failures always recorded, never silent. - Run controls (pause/resume/stop via checkpointed waits), step timeline, execution log, per-run cost estimates preferring provider-reported cost. - Human review workflow on claims (accept / reject / needs research) and on follow-up questions (suggested → approved), with bounded follow-up loops (max 3/project). - Solid security posture: RLS on all 10 tables with per-command policies, atomic run-launch DB function, service-role ownership guards in workers, server-only keys, count-based launch guards (3 active/project, 5/user, 25/project/day, 50/user/day), admin-gated deep mode, production refuses the mock provider. - CI (lint, typecheck, test, build) and ~8 test files on the critical guard paths.

### Corrections to earlier findings (verified live) - **The Perplexity endpoint is NOT a bug.** `POST https://api.perplexity.ai/v1/sonar` is the currently documented canonical chat-completions endpoint (verified against docs.perplexity.ai and by live 401-vs-404 HTTP probes; legacy `/chat/completions` is an older alias that still resolves). The code is more current than the reviewers' training data. - **Production does not silently fall back to mock.** `getResearchProviders()` throws in production unless `ALLOW_MOCK_PROVIDER=true` is explicitly set.

### Real gaps that remain | Gap | Severity | |---|---| | No live (un-mocked) provider smoke test — tests inject `fetchImpl`, so a broken provider integration is invisible by construction | High | | No production error monitoring (Sentry etc.) on Next.js or the Trigger.dev worker | High | | Launch guards are **count-only**; no dollar budgets. Worst case ~50 runs/day × ~$3 = ~$150/user/day COGS exposure with no billing in place | High | | No billing, export, sharing, notifications, onboarding, teams, API keys, webhooks | Required for launch (in that order — see plan) | | Research **modes are UI decoration**: `ResearchProviderInput` has no `modes` field; prompts never use them; follow-ups hardcode two modes | Medium | | The cross-run claims knowledge base — the strategic asset — is invisible in the run-centric UI | Medium | | `metadata` JSONB cast `as unknown as Json` without schema validation on read | Medium | | No rate limiting on server actions; no run-stuck timeout/heartbeat | Medium |

### The loop is commoditized | Provider | Offer | Cost | |---|---|---| | Google Gemini Deep Research API (Interactions API, Apr 2026) | full managed research agent | **~$2/task** (standard), ~$5 (Max) | | OpenAI Deep Research API | o4-mini / o3 | $0.41–$0.92 / ~$1.45 typical (to $30 heavy) | | Anthropic Managed Agents (beta Apr 2026) | hosted agent loop + "Outcomes" rubric-graded iterate→grade→revise (≤20 iterations), multi-agent coordination | $0.08/session-hr + tokens | | Perplexity Agent API + **Search as Code** | reasoning model writes sandboxed Python search pipelines; claims **85% token reduction** | tool-call pricing (web_search $0.005/call, sandbox $0.03/session) | | Tavily `/research` | managed research endpoint | $0.03–$2.00/request |
Perplexity Sonar API (current docs): Search API $5/1K requests; `sonar-deep-research` $2/M in, $8/M out, +$2/M citation, +$3/M reasoning, +$5/1K searches → **$0.41–$1.32 per query** measured.

**Implications:** (a) Anthropic's Managed Agents and Perplexity's Search-as-Code absorb exactly the orchestration plumbing ResearchLoop built on Trigger.dev — that layer is now a roadmap item for every platform, not a moat; (b) the same products are **falling-cost suppliers** if ResearchLoop keeps only the verification/persistence layer and treats backends as swappable; (c) Anthropic's June 15, 2026 move to dedicated agent credit pools at API rates normalizes usage-based agent pricing — aligning with credit-based pricing here.

### Phase 1 — Make it a deliverable (days 7–30) 6. **Export**: Markdown + PDF with the claims ledger, per-claim sources, evidence strength, review status, and a citation appendix. For the target buyer, the export *is* the product. 7. **Run-completion emails** (Resend) — runs take 5–30 min; users currently walk away into a void. 8. Onboarding sample project; Zod-validate `metadata` on read. 9. **Recruit 10–20 free design partners** (boutique consultants, mid-market CI practitioners, VC platform analysts). Instrument **claim acceptance rate** as the core metric.

### Phase 2 — Make it differentiated (days 31–60) 10. **Citation-verification pass** (the moat feature): fetch each source URL, verify resolution + claim support, stamp results on `sources`/`claims`, show a per-report verified-citations score. Sanitize fetched content against prompt injection. 11. **Wire modes into prompts** (add `modes` to `ResearchProviderInput`; collapse 5 modes → 3, flagship: `competitor_analysis` and `risks_sceptic_review` — the first maps to the Klue/Crayon WTP category, the second pairs uniquely with contradiction detection). 12. **Project-level claims knowledge-base view** (cross-run, filterable by status/strength/freshness) — make the Postgres asset visible. 13. Add a **Gemini Deep Research backend** behind the existing `ResearchProvider` interface (fixed ~$2/task unit cost) with per-run backend selection. 14. Publish a small **public accuracy benchmark** vs raw ChatGPT/Gemini deep research.

### Phase 3 — Make it sellable (days 61–90) 15. **Stripe credit billing**: Free 3 quick runs / Pro $49 / Team $199 as above; deep mode = 3 credits, Pro-only (replaces the ADMIN_EMAILS gate). 16. Read-only public share links for reports (cheap virality; full teams only when the $199 tier has buyers). 17. Positioning: **"Research you can sign your name to"** — verified citations, claim audit trail, persistent research memory. Two design-partner case studies. 18. Distribution: 10 public citation-audited sample reports as SEO pages; Show HN / Product Hunt; consulting + CI communities (SCIP, r/consulting, Indie Hackers); 2–3 consultant-newsletter slots. **No lifetime deals** (real per-run COGS makes LTDs toxic).

### Decision gates (pre-committed) - **Day 30:** measured avg COGS ≤ $1.50/run? ≥10 design partners with 3+ completed runs each? Claim acceptance >70% validates the trust thesis; <50% means the verification layer needs work before any paid launch. - **Day 90:** ≥100 signups and ≥3% free→paid conversion → continue. 2–3% → pivot to open-core BYO-key at $29/mo or per-deliverable pricing. <2% → stop; the asset becomes a portfolio piece / acquisition conversation (the verification pipeline + schema is a plausible feature-acquisition target for Klue/Crayon-tier vendors). - **Standing kill criteria:** Google/OpenAI ship claim-level structured citations with persistent project memory at the $20 tier; or platform-dependency maintenance consumes >50% of dev time for two consecutive weeks; or own measured citation accuracy is not materially better than the ~60%-error baseline.

### Handle before charging money (any phase) - **Liability & terms:** AI-research disclaimers in ToS; check Perplexity/OpenAI/Google terms on commercial resale of output; E&O exposure if a consultant resells a wrongly-"verified" claim; EU AI Act transparency obligations. - **Confidentiality:** customers' research questions reveal strategy — document provider data-retention/training opt-outs; this is a prerequisite for the compliance-sensitive buyer. - **Data freshness:** claims decay — timestamp, expire, and offer re-verification; a stale "verified" claim is a liability. - **Solo-founder vendor risk:** expect it as a sales objection (support SLAs, key-person risk), not just a capacity limit; status page + documented data export mitigate it partially.
